title: Oaths are latria-acts—yet swearing by Saints is allowed secondarily as divine truth shines in them (Thomas 2a2ae q.89 a.6)
source_text: XXXIV. Porro Theologi Ecclesiae Romanae juramentum etiam numerant inter actus Latriae, sive Religionis, id est, cultus qui soli Deo debetur. Et tamen in Ecclesia Romana usitatum est per Sanctos jurare. Verum dicunt Scholastici licere per Sanctos jurare, saltem secundario; nempe, quatenus in ipsis divina veritas elucet. Et ita per Sanctos jurari, non secundum se, sed in quantum veritatem divinam crediderunt & observarunt. Ut apud eundem Thomam videre est 2.2. quaest. 89. art. 6.
pass_a_gloss: Further the Theologians of the Roman Church also number the oath among the acts of Latria, or of Religion, that is, of the cult which is owed to God alone. And yet in the Roman Church it is customary to swear by the Saints. But the Scholastics say it is lawful to swear by the Saints, at least secondarily; namely, insofar as divine truth shines in them. And thus one swears by the Saints, not according to themselves, but insofar as they believed and observed the divine truth. As is to be seen in the same Thomas, 2a2ae, question 89, article 6.
pass_b_english: Oaths belong to latria—yet Rome swears by Saints.
Scholastics allow it secondarily: swear by the divine truth shining in them (Thomas 2a2ae q.89 a.6), not by the Saints as such.

choices.why: Ground of secondary swearing by Saints.
